# Feature: User-Provided Report Templates

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-004
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Today every synthesized output converges on the protocol `Brief`: answer-first
overview, key findings, sections, numbered sources. That default stays. This
feature adds a second, **opt-in** shape: the user supplies a Markdown template
describing the report they actually want — an exec brief, a weekly status, a
vendor comparison — and Yantra produces exactly that document instead of a Brief.

Templates are **saveable, taggable, and reusable**: `yantra template new|save|
list|show|lint|remove` manages a local library, and `ask`/`research`/`do` accept
`--template <ref>` naming a file path, a saved name, or a tag.

**LLM-only.** A template describes prose a model must write; the deterministic
synthesizer has no path to it. `--template` combined with `--no-llm` (or
`LLM_PROVIDER=none`) is a **validation failure**, not a silent degrade.

### The central design decision

The obvious implementation — paste the template into the prompt, ask for Markdown
back, hope — trades away every guarantee `result_publish` currently provides. This
feature does not do that. Instead:

> **The model never writes the template's structure.** Yantra parses the template
> into a **slot manifest**, generates a TypeBox schema from that manifest, and
> makes it `result_publish`'s parameter schema. The model fills named slots; the
> **runtime renders the template**. Structural deviation is not "discouraged by
> prompt wording" — it is unrepresentable.

This preserves what the Brief path already earned: provider-level missing-field
surfacing before the call runs, structured correctable errors, the bounded retry
loop, ledger-authoritative sources, and inert HTML artifacts.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules (coding standards, layering, testing, logging, security) are in
> `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

**Template document** — Markdown with optional YAML frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: exec-brief
description: Weekly executive brief
tags: [work, weekly]
---

# {{ title }}

## Executive Summary

{{ summary | markdown, max_words=200 }}

## Key Risks

{{ risks | list, min=3, max=5 }}

## Vendor Comparison

{{ comparison | table(Vendor, Price, Notes) }}

## Sources

{{ sources }}
```

**Five slot kinds.** `text` (single-line), `markdown` (multi-paragraph prose,
the default when no kind is given), `list` (string array → `- ` bullets),
`table(Col, Col, …)` (row array → GFM table), and the reserved `sources`
(engine-owned; the model can never fill it, so it can never courier a URL).

**`title` is special but model-filled**: when the template declares `{{ title }}`
its value becomes the document title used by history, terminal rendering, and the
HTML `<title>`. Templates without it get a title derived from the template name.

**Parse → manifest → generated schema.** The parser records each slot's key, kind,
constraints, and **enclosing heading path**. That heading path becomes the
generated schema's `description` for the slot — it is how the model learns what
`summary` means without any hand-written per-template prompt:

```ts
Type.Object({
  report: Type.Object(
    {
      title: Type.String({ minLength: 1, description: 'Document title. Required.' }),
      summary: Type.String({
        description: 'Content for "Executive Summary". Markdown prose, at most 200 words.',
      }),
      risks: Type.Array(Type.String(), {
        minItems: 3,
        maxItems: 5,
        description: 'Content for "Key Risks". 3-5 short plain-text items.',
      }),
      comparison: Type.Array(Type.Array(Type.String()), {
        description:
          'Content for "Vendor Comparison". Rows of exactly 3 cells: Vendor, Price, Notes.',
      }),
    },
    { additionalProperties: false },
  ),
});
```

**Same tool name.** The generated schema replaces `BriefContentParams` on the
existing `result_publish` tool rather than introducing a second tool. The
`actionPhase` single-publication latch, the completion nudge, `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`,
and the outcome plumbing all reference `result_publish` by name; a parallel tool
would fork every one of them.

**Four validation layers**, all returning correctable errors through the existing
retry loop (`REPORT_INVALID`, mirroring `BRIEF_INVALID`):

1. **Provider-level** — the generated schema surfaces a named missing or
   mistyped slot _before the call executes_.
2. **Constraints JSON Schema cannot express** — `max_words`/`min_words`, table
   row arity against the declared column count.
3. **Anti-hallucination** — every inline `[n]` marker must resolve to a declared
   ledger source; any URL in a slot value that is not in the ledger is rejected.
   This is the templated equivalent of the existing `urlHint` remedy.
4. **Hygiene** — no raw ANSI escape bytes (reuses the Brief rule), no echoed
   `{{ … }}` placeholder syntax inside slot values.

**Provenance is reused verbatim.** The new `TemplatedReport` schema embeds
`BriefSource[]`, `BriefMetadata`, and `BriefNotice[]` unchanged, so the
ledger-authoritative sources rule, the audit trail, and `history-store`'s
`metadata.usage.cost_usd` read all keep working with no special-casing.

**No new dependencies.** `marked`, `yaml`, and `prompts` are already in
`@yantra/core`; `renderReport(markdown, opts)` already exists on `OutputRenderer`;
the inert-HTML machinery already exists in `brief/to-html.ts` and is extracted for
reuse rather than reimplemented.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **Artifact family is `document.*`, not `report.*`.** `report.md` is already the
  per-run audit/trust report written by `FilesystemReportBuilder` and surfaced by
  `yantra report <run-id>`. Templated runs write
  `document.json` / `document.md` / `document.html` alongside it. `brief.*` stays
  Brief-only — an artifact named `brief.json` that does not validate as a Brief
  would be a trap for every future reader, and `history-store` would silently
  record a null `brief_id`.

- **`--detail` is inert in template mode.** The template dictates depth. Passing
  `--detail` explicitly alongside `--template` emits a one-line stderr warning
  rather than being silently ignored. `--format` and `--length` keep working
  (`--length` is _also_ inert and warned the same way — the template's
  constraints are the length budget).

- **No runtime-assembled fallback in template mode.**
  `maybeAssembleUnpublishedResult` packages an unpublished agent's final draft
  prose into a Brief. Slots cannot be honestly reverse-engineered from prose, so
  in template mode that path is skipped and the run ends `AGENT_COMPLETION_MISSING`.
  Inventing a filled template would be worse than failing.

- **`PublishedBriefRef` is widened, not renamed.** It gains a
  `kind: 'brief' | 'templated_report'` discriminator; the outcome field stays
  `outcome.brief` so the change does not ripple across orchestrator, outcome, and
  three CLI commands. The field name is documented as historical.

### Explicitly out of scope

- **`run` / saved workflows.** Deferred to a follow-up spec: workflow
  `synthesis.template`, threading through `LlmSynthesizer`, `do --save-as`
  promotion carrying the template, and the scheduled-fire degrade-with-notice
  behavior. Per `.spec-lite/memory.md`, that mode must live in the saved
  workflow artifact rather than being a per-invocation flag, which is a schema +
  promotion change large enough to stand alone. TASK-010 registers `--template`
  on `run` with a pointed "not yet supported" error so users are not met with a
  bare commander unknown-option message.
- Template variables bound to run data (params, captures, dates). Slots are
  model-filled only.
- Template sharing, remote fetch, or a template registry.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store — this is filesystem + protocol schemas, consistent with
workflows, profiles, and run artifacts.

### Entities & Attributes

- **ReportTemplate** (on disk: `<templatesRoot()>/<name>.md`, one file, self-describing)
  - `name` (string) — slug; `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, unique, = filename stem
  - `description` (string | null) — one-line human summary
  - `tags` (string[]) — normalized lowercase slugs, deduped, sorted; may be empty
  - `body` (string) — the Markdown template text below the frontmatter

- **TemplateManifest** (parsed, in-memory; protocol schema)
  - `name` / `description` / `tags` — as above
  - `slots` (TemplateSlot[]) — declaration order
  - `body` (string) — retained verbatim for rendering
  - `hash` (string) — SHA-256 of the raw template text, stamped into the document
    for auditability

- **TemplateSlot**
  - `key` (string) — `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$`, unique within a template
  - `kind` (`'text' | 'markdown' | 'list' | 'table' | 'sources'`) — default `markdown`
  - `headingPath` (string[]) — enclosing ATX headings, outermost first; drives the
    generated schema description
  - `columns` (string[] | null) — non-null only for `table`
  - `constraints` — `{ minChars?, maxChars?, minWords?, maxWords?, min?, max? }`
  - `offset` (number) — character offset in `body`, for deterministic rendering

- **TemplatedReport** (protocol schema; persisted as `document.json`)
  - `report_id` (ULID) — unique document id
  - `task_id` (ULID) — originating task
  - `schema_version` (literal `'0.2'`) — tracks the protocol version
  - `template` — `{ name: string | null, source: 'saved' | 'path', path: string | null, hash: string }`
  - `title` (string, min 1)
  - `slots` (Record<string, SlotValue>) — `SlotValue = string | string[] | string[][]`
  - `rendered_md` (string) — the canonical rendered document; `document.md` is this
    plus a trailing newline
  - `sources` (BriefSource[]) — **reused verbatim from the Brief schema**
  - `metadata` (BriefMetadata) — **reused verbatim**; `synthesis: 'llm'` always
  - `notices` (BriefNotice[]) — **reused verbatim**

### Relationships

- ReportTemplate 1:N TemplatedReport via `template.name` (a _reference_, not a
  copy — editing a saved template changes future reports; `template.hash` records
  which revision produced a given document)
- TemplatedReport 1:N BriefSource via the engine-owned `sources` array

### Indexes & Constraints

- Template name uniqueness is enforced by the filesystem (`<name>.md`); `save`
  without `--force` raises `TemplateCollisionError`, mirroring
  `WorkflowCollisionError`
- Slot `key` uniqueness enforced at parse time — a duplicate is a parse error, not
  a last-one-wins
- `sources` is a **reserved key**: a template declaring it with any kind other
  than the implicit `sources` kind is a parse error, and it never appears in the
  generated schema
- Every `table` slot value row must have `length === columns.length`
- Every `[n]` in any slot value must satisfy `1 <= n <= sources.length`
- Listing is a directory scan sorted by mtime descending, matching
  `FileWorkflowStore.list()`

## 5. Dependencies

- **None new.** `marked`, `yaml`, `prompts`, `zod` are already `@yantra/core`
  dependencies; `typebox` is already an `@yantra/agent` dependency.
- Existing infrastructure this builds on: the evidence ledger
  (`RunServices.evidence`), the `actionPhase` latch, `BriefSource`/`BriefMetadata`/
  `BriefNotice`, `openArtifact`, `FileWorkflowStore` (as the store pattern), and
  `InteractiveConfirmationGateway`'s `prompts` usage (as the prompt pattern).

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A directly — templates add no credential surface. Template mode
  requires a provider session, which resolves through the existing
  `selectAgentSession` path (`--provider`/`--model`/`--thinking`/`--auth-secret`)
  with no changes.

- **Error Handling**: Three distinct classes, each mapped to the documented exit
  codes. **Validation (exit 1)**: unparseable template, unknown/ambiguous
  `--template` reference, `--template` with `--no-llm`, `--template` on `run`.
  All resolve _before_ the try block so no run directory is created.
  **Correctable (in-loop)**: slot validation failures return `REPORT_INVALID` with
  `retryable: true` and structured issues, feeding the existing bounded re-prompt
  loop; the action phase stays open so a corrected retry can succeed.
  **Execution (exit 2)**: the agent never publishes → `AGENT_COMPLETION_MISSING`,
  with no runtime assembly in template mode. Artifact write failure is reported as
  a schema-shaped error, matching `writeBriefArtifacts`' existing contract.

- **Logging**: Structured Pino only; **template body text is never logged** — it
  is user-authored and may contain sensitive framing. Log the template `name`,
  `hash`, `source`, and slot count. `tool-calls.jsonl` records the
  `result_publish` lifecycle as it does today; the run manifest gains
  `template: { name, hash, source }` so an audit can tell which template produced
  a given `document.*`.

- **Security**: Slot values are model-authored and derive from untrusted web
  content, so `document.html` goes through the **same** escape-before-parse inert
  pipeline as `brief.html` — extracted and shared, not reimplemented. The
  `sources` slot is engine-owned, keeping the ledger-authoritative rule intact:
  the model still never couriers a URL. Non-ledger URLs in slot values are
  rejected. Template files are read from user-specified paths — read-only, never
  executed, never interpolated as shell or code, and the parser is a pure
  string-to-manifest function with no I/O.
